_note: Trade Surveillance scenario library (AUR-J-SURV-001, WS-2.4). This is genuine new work — unlike the prior three Tier 2 roles, no detection signals existed in code. Each scenario declares severity (REVIEW -> flag for human review; ESCALATE -> halt + dual authority + potential regulatory reporting), an enabled flag, the record fields it requires, and detection parameters. DOCTRINAL INVARIANT: a flagged pattern is NEVER auto-disposed by the system — only human review clears it. A missing required field for an ENABLED scenario means the check could not run, which routes to SURVEIL_DATA_INCOMPLETE (cannot certify clean). Editing this fixture is a doctrine event. Fixed-income / Argus scope.

WASH_TRADE.label: Wash trade — no change in beneficial ownership
WASH_TRADE.regulatory_anchor: MAR Art. 12; MiFID II; SEC 10b-5; CFTC anti-wash

MARKING_THE_CLOSE.label: Marking the close — outsized volume in the closing window
MARKING_THE_CLOSE.detect: match if seconds_to_close <= close_window_seconds AND session_volume_pct >= volume_pct_threshold

FRONT_RUNNING.label: Front running — proprietary trade ahead of a known client order
FRONT_RUNNING.regulatory_anchor: FINRA 5270; MiFID II conflicts of interest

UNUSUAL_PRICE_DEVIATION.label: Execution price deviates from prevailing reference

CONCENTRATED_COUNTERPARTY.label: Single counterparty concentration in session flow

LAYERING_SPOOFING.label: Layering / spoofing — non-bona-fide orders then cancel
LAYERING_SPOOFING.declared_not_active_reason: Requires order-book / order-lifecycle event data not in the Argus deployment scope. Declared in the library so activation is a fixture flip, not a schema change, once order data is available.
